content:
iOS 27 beta 5 further expands the new Siri voice customization options. In the earlier beta versions, the newly added "Speech Rate" and "Expressiveness" sliders were only available for the two new American-accented Siri voices.

However, the customization features are now available for any American-accented voice, as well as all existing British-accented voices...

This means there are now a total of eleven supported voices that allow you to choose different Speech Rate (how fast the voice speaks) and Expressiveness (emotion and emphasis level) settings.

You can go to "Settings" → "Siri" → "Voice," and drag the sliders to customize the "Speech Rate" and "Expressiveness" — each has five supported levels.

On the newer iPhone models, a total of eight American-accented and four British-accented voice options are available, all of which support Speech Rate and Expressiveness adjustments.

Apple previously stated that the new Siri voice uses a brand-new powerful on-device model, but it requires relatively new hardware. This feature requires iPhone 17 Pro, iPhone 17 Air, iPad Pro (M4) or newer models, as well as a Mac equipped with an M3 chip or newer with at least 12GB of RAM.

Siri AI itself requires an iPhone 15 Pro or newer model; on older hardware, it will only use the older voice synthesis technology. Siri AI will be launched in beta later this year.
